question: During the hearing before the Committee on Economic Affairs on 10 September 2026 in Parliament, the Commission stated that further European integration of banking supervision is necessary to facilitate cross-border banking activities and to complete the Banking Union. At the same time, it acknowledged that Member States are concerned about the implications of greater flexibility regarding the holding of capital and liquidity outside the home Member State. 1.

How will the Commission ensure that further European integration of banking supervision and greater flexibility regarding cross-border capital and liquidity flows do not result in national taxpayers ultimately bearing the financial risks of banking activities carried out elsewhere in the Union?

What specific safeguards will the Commission put in place to ensure that the principle of risk-sharing within the Banking Union is accompanied by a proportionate allocation of responsibility and liability for those risks, including within a bank or banking group?
How does the Commission view the further development and supervision of the interdependence between banks and states in the case of larger, cross-border banks?
